objections.title: Can't afford it
root_causes: Lack of understanding of program cost
questions: When you say it's not affordable right now, is that about the fee itself, or about how it's structured?
What would need to be true for this to feel affordable?
Help me understand what 'afford' means for you here — is it the total, or the monthly?
facts: Timeshare exit fees are typically one-time or short-financed costs, distinct from perpetual annual maintenance fee obligations.
Maintenance fees on most timeshare contracts are contractually obligated for as long as the deed or membership is held, including by heirs unless formally released.
follow_ups: Run True Cost of Ownership calculator together
Show comparison vs. continuing to own
Offer financing structure comparison

objections.title: Need to think about it
questions: When you say you need to think about it, what specifically do you want to think through?
Of everything we covered, what's the one part that isn't sitting right yet?
If that one thing weren't a question mark anymore, would you feel ready to move forward?
facts: Most owners who defer a decision without naming a specific concern report the maintenance fee obligation continued to accrue in the interim.
follow_ups: Ask a clarifying discovery question before ending the call
Offer a written summary of the plan to think over
Schedule a specific follow-up time, not 'later'

objections.title: Too expensive
root_causes: Comparing exit cost to wrong baseline (should compare to lifetime ownership cost)
questions: Expensive compared to what — the timeshare payments you're already making, or something else?
What number were you expecting, and where does that number come from?
facts: A cost comparison should weigh the exit fee against the total remaining lifetime cost of ownership, not against zero.
follow_ups: Run Comparison vs Exiting calculator
Break total cost into a monthly-equivalent figure

objections.title: Need to talk to spouse
root_causes: Genuine need for joint financial decision
questions: What do you think your spouse's first question is going to be?
Would it help to get them on this call, or a follow-up call, so I can answer that directly?
Is there anything about this you're unsure how to explain to them?
follow_ups: Offer a 3-way follow-up call
Send a written summary made for a spouse who wasn't on the call

objections.title: Want to save money first
questions: What's the timeline you're picturing to save that amount?
In that time, what happens with the maintenance fee bill that's still coming?
facts: Waiting to save toward an exit fee typically means the annual maintenance fee obligation continues to accrue in parallel.
follow_ups: Show Maintenance Fee Inflation calculator for the waiting period
Discuss financing structures that don't require saving up front

objections.title: Sounds too good to be true
root_causes: Prior bad experience with timeshare industry itself
questions: What have you tried before, or heard about, that didn't work out?
What would you need to see to feel confident this is legitimate?
What specifically feels too good — the process, the price, or the outcome?
facts: Timeshare owners are frequently targeted by unrelated resale and exit scams, which is a reasonable basis for caution and worth taking seriously rather than dismissing.
follow_ups: Offer documentation and BBB profile
Offer to connect with a past client for a reference
Provide the process broken into concrete steps

objections.title: Never heard of your company
root_causes: Lack of familiarity, not necessarily suspicion
questions: What sources do you usually trust to check out a company like this?
Would seeing our BBB profile and client reviews help?
follow_ups: Share BBB rating and profile link
Share review sources
Offer company background in writing

objections.title: Need to research first
questions: What specifically are you hoping to find when you research this?
Is there a particular concern driving the research, or is this just your normal process for a decision like this?
follow_ups: Point to specific, verifiable sources rather than leaving it open-ended
Offer to follow up at a set time after they've had a chance to look

objections.title: Is this legit?
questions: What would answer that question for you — documentation, reviews, licensing, something else?
Has something specific made you doubt it, or is this just a standard check?
follow_ups: Provide documentation directly, without defensiveness
Offer a reference client

objections.title: Want attorney review
questions: Is there a specific clause or concern you'd want an attorney to look at, or is this a general step you take on contracts?
Would it help if I sent the documents ahead so your attorney has time before we talk again?
facts: Reviewing exit or transfer documents with independent counsel before signing is a reasonable step for any contract of this kind.
follow_ups: Send documents proactively
Schedule follow-up after their review window

objections.title: Worried about credit damage
root_causes: Lack of understanding of how the exit process interacts with credit
questions: What have you heard specifically about credit and timeshare exits?
Is the concern about the exit process itself, or about what happens if the maintenance fees go unpaid?
facts: Unpaid maintenance fees or special assessments can be referred to collections by a resort or HOA, which can affect credit — this is a resort-side risk of nonpayment, not something the exit process itself causes.
Credit impact, when it occurs in these situations, generally traces to delinquency reporting by the resort or its collection agency, not to a properly documented, resort-acknowledged exit.
follow_ups: Explain the documented exit process step-by-step
Clarify what would and would not appear on a credit report

objections.title: Afraid of being sued
root_causes: Confusion about resort remedies for nonpayment
questions: What specifically are you picturing when you think about a lawsuit?
Has a resort or collection agency already contacted you about this, or is this a concern about the future?
facts: Resorts and HOAs can pursue collection remedies for unpaid dues, which vary by state and by the resort's own governing documents.
A documented, acknowledged exit reduces ongoing exposure to future dues that could otherwise become collectible.
follow_ups: Explain what the exit documentation covers
Discuss state-specific collection remedies if relevant to their resort

objections.title: Worried about collections
root_causes: Existing delinquency they haven't fully disclosed
questions: Have you already been contacted by a collections agency about this account?
What's the current status of your maintenance fee payments?
facts: Collections activity is generally tied to unpaid fees and typically escalates the longer an account stays delinquent.
follow_ups: Get a clear, honest picture of current account standing before proceeding
Explain how the exit process addresses an existing delinquent account, if applicable

objections.title: Worried about passing it to heirs
root_causes: Genuine concern about family financial burden
questions: What made this become a concern for you — a conversation with family, something you read, or an estate planning step?
Do your heirs currently know they'd inherit this obligation?
facts: In most states, a deeded timeshare interest becomes part of the estate and can pass to heirs along with its ongoing maintenance fee obligation unless the heir formally disqualifies the inheritance.
There is generally a limited window after the owner's death during which an heir must act to disclaim the interest — the specific deadline is set by state probate law and the resort's own process.
follow_ups: Walk through the specific state's disclaimer window if known
Provide the heirs estate-liability explanation

objections.title: Worried about bankruptcy implications
root_causes: Broader financial distress beyond just the timeshare
questions: Is the timeshare part of a bigger financial picture you're working through right now?
Have you spoken with a bankruptcy attorney about how a timeshare obligation would be treated?
facts: How a timeshare debt is treated in a bankruptcy filing depends on the type of filing and jurisdiction — this is a legal question best answered by a bankruptcy attorney, not a general rule.
follow_ups: Avoid giving legal conclusions — recommend attorney consultation
Focus on what's factually documented about the contract itself

objections.title: Worried about tax implications
root_causes: Lack of clarity on how debt relief or exit is treated for tax purposes
questions: What specifically have you heard about taxes and timeshare exits?
Is this about property tax, income tax, or something else?
facts: Tax treatment of debt relief or transfer arrangements can vary by individual circumstances — this is a question for a licensed tax professional, not a blanket answer.
follow_ups: Recommend a CPA consultation for their specific situation
Provide only documented, factual process information

objections.title: Call me later
root_causes: Sometimes a soft objection in disguise
questions: Is there a specific time today or tomorrow that's better, or is 'later' more open-ended right now?
Is there anything about what we discussed that's giving you pause, separate from timing?
follow_ups: Lock a specific callback time, not an open-ended one
Send a short written recap before hanging up

objections.title: Too busy right now
questions: Would a shorter call at a set time work better than trying to finish this now?
On a scale of interest, how much do you want to solve this once time isn't the issue?
follow_ups: Offer a tightly time-boxed follow-up (10-15 min)
Send materials to review on their own time

objections.title: Currently on vacation
questions: When do you get back, and would that be a good time to pick this back up?
follow_ups: Schedule a specific follow-up date after their return

objections.title: Wants to wait until after the holidays
questions: Is the holiday timing about your schedule, or about holiday spending making this feel like a lot right now?
What happens with maintenance fee billing between now and after the holidays?
follow_ups: Show Maintenance Fee Inflation calculator for the deferral period
Set a firm specific follow-up date

objections.title: Waiting for next paycheck
questions: When's the paycheck you're referring to, so we can plan around it directly rather than leave it open-ended?
follow_ups: Discuss financing options that don't require full payment up front
Set specific follow-up date tied to pay date

objections.title: Needs husband's input
questions: What do you think his main question or concern is going to be?
Would a short call together work better than relaying secondhand?
follow_ups: Offer a joint follow-up call
Prepare a written summary aimed at answering his likely questions

objections.title: Needs wife's input
questions: What do you think her main question or concern is going to be?
Would a short call together work better than relaying secondhand?
follow_ups: Offer a joint follow-up call
Prepare a written summary aimed at answering her likely questions

objections.title: Worried about impact on kids' finances
questions: How does this fit into what you're already planning for your kids financially?
Is the concern about the cost of exiting, or about what happens if you keep paying maintenance fees for years to come?
follow_ups: Run 10/20/30-year cost projection to compare with the exit cost

objections.title: It's actually my parents' timeshare
root_causes: Often tied to inheritance/estate planning concerns
questions: Are you managing this on their behalf, or are they part of the conversation too?
Is there a health or estate planning timeline driving this?
follow_ups: Confirm who has legal authority to act on the account (POA, owner, etc.) before proceeding
Cross-reference with inheritance fear objection if relevant
